To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we present an algorithm, deployment order, that can be used to determine the location of nodes in a sensornet, (2) deployment order can be used to create a logical topology that allows nodes to determine their location in relation to other nodes, and (3) deployment order is simple to use, requiring only the user to specify a small number of locations in the network.
logical location determination and the "follow-me application" are possible with minimal user intervention.
we present a novel distributed algorithm for logical location determination that can be used in a wide range of sensornet applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of infrastructureless location determination techniques for sensor networks.
how to use sensor networks for applications that require location awareness, and how to do this in a completely distributed and infrastructureless manner.
the development of a novel infrastructure-less location aware configuration for wireless sensor networks, with applications to guidance systems and other location-aware applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the deployment order algorithm provides a novel, infrastructureless approach for determining logical locations in a distributed manner, and that it can be used to build sensornets for applications where physical location is not critical, such as the follow-me application.

this paper proposes a novel algorithm for logical location determination that exploits node deployment patterns to establish arbitrarily complex logical topology in a completely distributed and infrastructureless way.
the paper presents a novel algorithm that can establish arbitrarily complex sensor network topologies with minimal user interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an infrastructureless, self-organizing, and distributed system for logical location determination in sensor networks.
we present a new approach for logical location determination, which is based on deployment order and can be easily extended to physical location determination.
we have developed a novel infrastructureless location-aware configuration system for sensor networks that allows the deployment of sensornets in inhospitable environments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
logical locations are a viable alternative to physical locations for many applications.
the logical topology can be used to infer approximate physical location, which can then be used to infer physical topology.
logical locations can provide a simple and effective means for sensor networks to self-configure.
